review_notes: Read the whole target file (one theorem), Trace/Basic.lean, and Trace/Prod.lean and Trace/TensorProduct.lean in the same library. Mathlib has Module.Dual.transpose as a bundled linear map (Dual/Defs.lean:92) and LinearMap.prodMapLinear (Prod.lean:352). I did not check whether Mathlib already has an extensionality lemma for maps out of M →ₗ M that reduces to rank-one maps. I did not compile anything. The bundled maps and instance arguments for the Prod.lean uses (prodMap f 0 as a linear map of f) need checking, so the sketch there is untested. The file has only one proof, so the repetition is across files. It appears in Prod.lean twice with the same shape (lines 57–97), and twice more in modified form for the off-diagonal blocks (lines 163–180 and 191–208).

findings.problem: The proof reduces an equation between two additive functions of f : M →ₗ[R] M to rank-one maps. It does this by proving an auxiliary statement for every tensor t, running TensorProduct.inductionOn with a tmul case and an add case, and then pulling back along (dualTensorHomEquiv R M M).symm with dualTensorHom_dualTensorHomEquiv_symm. The same four-step scaffold (state the claim for dualTensorHom t, induct on t, discharge the add case by additivity, simpa back) appears in Trace/Prod.lean in traceOfFiniteProjective_prodMap_zero and traceOfFiniteProjective_zero_prodMap, and in modified form in traceOfFiniteProjective_inl_snd and traceOfFiniteProjective_inr_fst. In Prod.lean the add case is also hand-unrolled with prodMap_add and map_add rewrites. Each proof restates the same reduction, so the real content (the tmul computation) is buried in boilerplate.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma to Trace/Basic.lean, for example

theorem LinearMap.linearMap_ext_dualTensorHom {S : Type*} [AddCommMonoid S] [Module R S] {F G : (M →ₗ[R] M) →ₗ[R] S} (h : ∀ (φ : Module.Dual R M) (x : M), F (dualTensorHom R M M (φ ⊗ₜ[R] x)) = G (dualTensorHom R M M (φ ⊗ₜ[R] x))) : F = G

Proof sketch: (dualTensorHomEquiv R M M).surjective gives surjectivity of dualTensorHom R M M. Then F ∘ₗ dualTensorHom = G ∘ₗ dualTensorHom by TensorProduct.ext' and h, and LinearMap.cancel_right finishes. This ext lemma needs no Finite or Projective hypotheses and is stated for the bundled linear maps.

Use in Dual.lean: take F to be (traceOfFiniteProjective R (Module.Dual R M)) ∘ₗ (Module.Dual.transpose (R := R) (M := M) (M' := M)), which is bundled linear, and G to be traceOfFiniteProjective R M. After rw [dualMap_def], apply the lemma and keep only the current tmul computation: simp only [transpose_dualTensorHom, traceOfFiniteProjective_dualTensorHom, contractLeft_apply, Module.Dual.eval_apply]. The add case and the final simpa disappear.

Use in Prod.lean: take F to be trace(M×N) composed with the bundled linear map f ↦ prodMap f 0 (from LinearMap.prodMapLinear specialised, or an explicit LinearMap.mk), and G to be traceOfFiniteProjective R M. Keep only the existing tmul simp call. The N-side lemma is symmetric. The off-diagonal lemmas can use the same ext lemma with their tensor-specific hypotheses.
findings.benefit: The tensor induction, additivity and pull-back scaffold is written once and checked once. Each trace lemma then states only its rank-one computation, which makes the Dual and Prod proofs a few lines shorter. Prod.lean currently has about 20 near-duplicate lines per lemma, including hand-written add cases. A future trace-compatibility lemma (for example for base change) then needs only the tmul case.
